target_customer: Professional software developers working on large codebases
problem: Coding agents lose context and stall on long, hard tasks; Random Labs builds an agent meant to run for long hours on difficult problems.
business_model: developer tool, likely subscription or usage-based (not stated in sources)

founders.name: Kiran
founders.background_notes: YC lists the first name only; surname not confirmed by an opened source.

founders.name: Mihir Chintawar
founders.background_notes: No background found in opened sources.

technical_complexity.rationale: Orchestrating many model calls over million-line repositories with linked episodes (Thread Weaving) is hard agent engineering, though built on third-party models.

defensibility.rationale: Differentiation is orchestration architecture, which can be copied by Cursor, Claude Code and Codex; no published benchmarks as of review coverage.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: VentureBeat's March 2026 launch article positions Slate as a layer above Claude Code and OpenAI Codex rather than a rival; no dated source on direct copying.

market_need_then: AI coding assistants were in rapid adoption in 2024, and the YC page frames the need as long-running agents that work on hard problems; no quantified demand evidence found.

identity.visual_style: minimal site that returned almost no content to a fetch
identity.voice_and_tone: developer mission statement about keeping development in the hands of people

branding.brand_signature: Product name Slate and the swarm native claim
branding.community_and_virality: Open-source roots (GitHub org entropy-research per YC page) and VentureBeat coverage of the Slate V1 launch on 2026-03-12.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name with no sourced origin; the product name Slate gets the press, and Slate is also a common word.

outcome_analysis: Random Labs is an early stage YC Summer 2024 company that launched Slate V1 in March 2026 after an open beta. No funding beyond YC, no revenue and no exit were found, and the coding agent market is crowded with large funded players, so the outcome so far is unproven rather than successful or failed.
notes: Aggregators (VCBacked, startuphub) list 500K in total funding labeled pre-seed in 2024-09; unverified and likely the standard YC deal, so not recorded as a round. VentureBeat says funding not disclosed. Open source status of Slate conflicts between YC page and a GitHub commit. Kiran surname unconfirmed (a profile says Illindala). Competitor search found no sources dated near the 2024 batch, so list is empty; Cursor, Codex and Kilo Code appear only in 2026 reviews.
